subject: literature
passage: In her first week at the conservatory, Celestine heard Madame Roux tell the assembled students that correctness was "the virtue of a metronome" and that she had no wish to train metronomes. For the rest of the term, Madame Roux spent much of each class urging the students to take risks with phrasing, and she praised a boy named Anton, whose performances were often untidy, for his "daring." When Celestine finished her own piece at the last class of the term, every note in place, Madame Roux nodded, said that it was "perfectly correct," and turned to the next student. Celestine walked home slowly, the phrase echoing in her ears. The details of the text suggest that Madame Roux's comment on Celestine's performance was most likely ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: a sign that she considered Celestine the most gifted student she had ever taught.
choices.B: an admission that she had changed her mind about the importance of correctness.
choices.C: less approving than its words might seem on their own.
choices.D: an expression of disappointment that Celestine had played several wrong notes.

explanation.why: Connect the comment to Madame Roux's first-week remark. She called correctness "the virtue of a metronome" and said she had no wish to train metronomes, so calling Celestine's playing "perfectly correct" is faint praise at best. Celestine's slow walk home suggests she heard it that way too.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing suggests such high regard; Madame Roux's warmest praise that term went to Anton's daring, not to correctness.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text gives no sign that Madame Roux changed her view; her brief nod and quick move to the next student suggest she had not.
explanation.C: Correct. Because Madame Roux had dismissed correctness as a metronome's virtue, calling the performance "perfectly correct" was likely faint praise.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says every note was in place, so the comment cannot be about wrong notes.
